basis: Drug-resistant tuberculosis predominantly arises in and damages the lungs; resistance does not establish additional organ involvement.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: the lungs are the predominant disease site; drug resistance changes susceptibility, not the principal anatomical location.

basis: Intellectual disability and choanal atresia define syndrome; anal atresia and polydactyly each occur in 30-79%; unspecified eye/GU abnormalities do not establish functional damage.

decisions.ocular: none: the 30-79% annotation specifies only an eye abnormality, without establishing a damaging structural lesion or loss of function.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: postaxial polydactyly is a direct skeletal developmental defect reported in 30-79%; occasional joint and hip abnormalities are insufficient independently.

basis: Developmental delay and characteristic ocular/eyelid abnormalities define the phenotype; ptosis and blepharophimosis occur in 80-99%. Renal and cardiac abnormalities occur in 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: primary: characteristic eye-region abnormalities are explicitly defining; ptosis and blepharophimosis occur in 80-99%, supporting substantive eyelid involvement.

basis: Central/peripheral neural tumors and cutaneous neurofibromas define this historical phenotype; common hearing dysfunction is not established, and Lisch nodules are non-damaging.

decisions.otologic: none: vestibular schwannomas establish neural tumors, but the supplied evidence does not establish hearing or vestibular organ dysfunction in at least 30%.

basis: Postinfectious inflammation with defining cardiac dysfunction/shock; acute kidney injury occurs in roughly 40% as part of multisystem dysfunction. GI symptoms alone do not establish damage.

decisions.renal: involved: acute kidney injury occurs in approximately 40% and represents renal functional injury during the multisystem inflammatory illness.

basis: Immune-mediated skin and oral mucosal necrosis define disease; ocular surface dysfunction occurs in 30-79%. Airway abnormalities reported in 30-79% are omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: destruction of mucous membranes is explicitly defining, and oral mucosal blistering is a characteristic manifestation affecting the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Intellectual disability, pyloric stenosis and cranial skeletal abnormalities define syndrome; craniosynostosis occurs in 30-79%. Cryptorchidism is reproductive.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: brachycephaly is a named defining feature, supported by craniosynostosis in 30-79%, establishing a substantive cranial skeletal disorder.

basis: Characteristic cutaneous phenotype includes cafe-au-lait macules in 6/6; associated cancers are separately diagnosed diseases, not assumed organ damage. Lisch nodules are non-damaging.

decisions.haematologic: none: hematologic malignancies are separately diagnosed cancers arising from predisposition; the syndrome does not itself establish blood or marrow damage.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: colorectal cancer is a separately diagnosed consequence of cancer predisposition, even though reported in 1/2 annotated patients.
decisions.neurologic: none: astrocytoma and glioblastoma are separately diagnosed tumors; their risk or occurrence does not establish intrinsic neurologic involvement of the syndrome.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic cafe-au-lait macules in 6/6 and axillary freckling in 2/2 establish the syndrome's cutaneous phenotype.

basis: Hypospadias and urogenital sinus anomalies occur in 80-99% and directly affect urethral anatomy; reproductive tissue differences alone do not establish endocrine dysfunction.

decisions.renal: primary: frequent hypospadias and urogenital sinus malformations establish congenital urethral involvement; the urethra belongs to the renal axis.

basis: Disseminated choroidal and retinal inflammation encompasses infectious and immune-mediated uveitis; disseminated describes ocular distribution, not systemic spread.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: chorioretinitis encompasses infectious and immune-mediated inflammation of the choroid and retina, supporting the mechanism axis.
